newsitem.title: THAILAND: Pressure on Thai baht seen easing after float.
newsitem.headline: Pressure on Thai baht seen easing after float.

text.p: The widely-approved Bank of Thailand decision to float the baht on Wednesday will ease pressure on the currency, halt capital outflows and give the battered stock market a long-awaited lift, analysts said.

The baht was quoted 15-20 percent lower in offshore markets late on Wednesday at a rate of 28.80/29.60 following the early morning announcement by the central bank. In the domestic market it was at 27.50/28.50 to the dollar.

"This is a victory for economic pragmatism over vested political and business interests. The Bank of Thailand finally did the right thing when it had its back to the wall," said Mike Stead of Union Securities Plc.

The central bank let the baht float amid growing calls by leading local economists this week for an up to 15 percent devaluation which, they said, was essential in plugging drains on capital and foreign reserves seen in the past few months. Thai foreign reserves fell $4.0 billion in May after the Bank of Thailand defended the baht against market speculative attacks. Economists said they expected Thailand's $33.3 billion in foreign reserves to have been steadily eroded further if it had resisted a baht devaluation in the months ahead.

"Thailand would have been stripped naked if it delayed a devaluation for another three to six months," said Ammar Siamwala, senior economist at Thailand Development Research Institute, shortly before the central bank announcement.

Mark Sundburg, chief economist of Salomon Brothers in Hong Kong, said: "They were at a stage where they didn't have much choice because of the domestic liquidity crisis and their inability to reduce domestic interest rates. "The spectre of widespread business bankruptcies or failures in a sense forced their hands. It was a question of timing. They were looking to move to a more flexible exchange rate system," he said. The central bank's decision spurred

the Thai bourse to rally 7.87 percent at the Wednesday close. Puthiporn Nakornchai of HG Asia said active foreign stock bargain hunting after the baht float announcement should boost the composite SET Index to at least 600 points soon.

"I think the market has already seen its bottom. The float is a face-saving move by the central bank in removing doubt about the baht direction even though it could not brighten other bearish fundamentals," she said.
Her colleague Philip Korsawadigul said: "I agree with the central bank decision. Short-term gains are essential for the sake of long-term recovery."

Analysts, however, remained wary that the economy, growing at its slowest pace in a decade this year and faced with major troubles in the finance and property sectors, may still not come out of the woods. "The economy has so many imponderables, including high non-performing loans of the finance sector and property sector problems," Stead said. Analysts said they were anxious to see where the central bank wanted the baht to settle. The bank said on Wednesday it would intervene occasionally if necessary in the future to defend the currency.
"The central bank must have a range for the baht in mind and the market would like to know what it is," a foreign analyst said.
